group_assessment.weighting: A Greek paediatric neurology and metabolic group reporting two siblings; descriptive clinical, with CSF folate measured in a reference laboratory. Not a WWOX group; the paper is a SUBSTITUTE for the folate axis (class level, not WWOX evidence). Observations (variants, CSF values, imaging, seizure counts) are weighed above the treatment-benefit interpretation, which the authors themselves call difficult to interpret.

entries.proposition: NOT WWOX EVIDENCE (substitute, disease class). The younger sibling's CSF 5-MTHF at diagnosis was 49 nmol/L, far above the under-5 typical of FOLR1 deficiency, which the authors take to mean that moderately low CSF folate cannot separate a primary folate-receptor defect from secondary deficiency.
entries.snippet: 5‐MTHF levels of younger sibling were also higher compared to previous patients with FOLR1 deficiency (usually <5 nmol/L).

experimental_context.system: two siblings with compound heterozygous FOLR1 variants (class level: cerebral folate transport deficiency); NOT a WWOX system
experimental_context.endpoint: CSF 5-MTHF, MRI, EEG, seizure counts under treatment

entries.proposition: The older sibling's CSF value (19 nmol/L) was taken while on oral folinic acid, so the two siblings' CSF values are not comparable at baseline, and the reference range quoted for the younger sibling differs between sentences (63-122 at diagnosis, 44-122 at repeat).
entries.snippet: The CSF collection and analysis were identical between siblings; the older sister was under treatment with per os calcium folinate at diagnosis.

entries.proposition: The ketogenic-diet effect is a halving of daily seizures (about 10 to 5) in one child after add-on to two antiseizure drugs, in a seizure course that fluctuated between 10 and 15 per day beforehand; other changes (vitamin B6, folic acid, folinic acid) overlap in time.
entries.snippet: Ketogenic diet (KD), initiated 3 months after seizure onset as an add‐on treatment to valproate and topiramate, resulted in a further 50% reduction of seizure frequency (approximately 10 episodes per day reduced to 5 per day) and severity with a significant improvement in the patient's daily life.

entries.proposition: The authors themselves say the benefit of folinic acid in the older sibling cannot be separated from the ketogenic diet and the antiseizure drugs.
entries.snippet: The benefit of folinic acid supplementation reported in the case of the older sibling is difficult to be interpreted, as it was administered in combination with ketogenic diet and antiepileptic treatment.

entries.proposition: One of the two FOLR1 variants is a novel missense variant classed as of uncertain significance; pathogenicity rests on in silico tools, phenotype, low CSF folate and segregation.
